out.other_title: Open question: helpfulness and instruction-following without any human feedback
out.rationale: Bai et al. leave open whether helpfulness and instruction-following can be achieved without human feedback. Wen et al. label 5,000 'more helpful, harmless, and honest' pairs with ICM, train a reward model and run RL for 250,000 episodes, reporting the assistant matches its human-label counterpart on average (higher chat and safety, lower math and code); scoring used a production-grade Claude 4 Opus reward model.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether an assistant can be trained for helpfulness without human preference labels, using an unsupervised reward model on a Claude 4 Sonnet base

text: The paper reports building 5,000 pairwise preference examples with the description 'Output A is more helpful, harmless, and honest than Output B', labeling them with the authors' method using Claude 4 Sonnet pretrained models, and training a reward model, compared against one trained on production-grade human labels. After RL on 250,000 episodes and scoring on RewardBench by a production-grade Claude 4 Opus reward model, the unsupervised assistant matches its human-supervised counterpart on average, scoring higher on chat and safety and lower on math and code.
title: Assistant RL-trained on unsupervised-label reward model matches human-supervised counterpart on average on RewardBench
